title: Palay: Meaning, Parts, Growth Stages and How It Becomes Rice
metaTitle: Palay: Meaning, Growth Stages and Palay to Rice
metaDescription: Palay is rice still in its husk. Learn palay in English, the parts of the grain, each growth stage from seed to harvest, and how palay becomes rice.
excerpt: Palay is rice that still wears its husk. It is the grain you harvest, dry and sell before any mill touches it. This guide explains what palay means in English and names the parts of the grain. It also follows the plant from seed to harvest and shows how the grain turns into the rice on your table.

heroImage.alt: Ripe palay heads bending over in a rice field

blocks.text: In the field we use three words for one grain. Palay is the crop and the unmilled grain, bigas is milled rice, and kanin is cooked rice. The price changes at each step, so a farmer who knows palay well, from seed class to moisture, sells better and loses less.
Palay meaning and palay in English

Palay in English is paddy, rough rice or unhusked rice. So if someone asks for the English ng palay, any of the three works. PhilRice and the PSA write it as palay (unhusked rice) in their reports. In daily talk, though, the palay meaning goes wider. Farmers say palay for the growing plant, the ripe heads and the sacks of dried grain.

A related word is palayan, the rice field itself. The widest palayan areas lie in Central Luzon. Nueva Ecija even took the word for its capital, as our story on [Palayan, Nueva Ecija](/blog/palayan-nueva-ecija) explains.

Many farm towns also celebrate the crop. For example, Narra in Palawan, known as the rice granary of that province, holds a Palay Festival every mid or late October. The old stories live on too. Our page on the [alamat ng palay](/blog/alamat-ng-palay) retells the legend and gives a short buod and banghay for students.
Parts of the palay grain
Open one grain with your thumbnail and you will see why milling matters. Each grain of palay rice has four parts.

items: **Hull or husk (ipa).** The hard outer cover. FAO puts it at about 20 percent of the weight of palay, with a range of 16 to 28 percent.
**Bran (darak).** The thin brown layers under the hull. The mill takes it off with the germ.
**Germ or embryo.** The small living part at one end. It sprouts when you sow the seed.
**Endosperm.** The white, starchy core. This is the bigas you cook.

blocks.text: Take off the hull and you get brown rice. Then polish away the bran and germ and you get white milled rice. The small broken bits from the mill go to market as binlid.
Growth stages of palay from seed to harvest

IRRI splits the life of the rice plant into three phases. In the tropics the reproductive phase takes about 35 days and ripening about 30 days. So the vegetative phase decides if a variety is early or late. For example, IR64 matures in 110 days with a 45 day vegetative phase, while IR8 needs 130 days with a 65 day vegetative phase.
Vegetative phase: seed, seedlings and tillers

This phase runs from germination to panicle initiation. First the seed swells and sends out a root and a shoot. Then the palay seedlings grow leaves and, after transplanting, send out tillers. These side shoots later carry the heads, so most of your fertilizer and weeding work happens here.
Reproductive phase: panicle to flowering

Inside the stem a tiny panicle forms. Next the stem grows longer, the flag leaf appears and the leaf sheath swells, which farmers call booting. After that the head pushes out and the flowers open. PalayCheck warns that drought from panicle initiation to grain filling leaves many empty grains.
Ripening phase: milk, dough and mature grain

At first the grain fills with a milky liquid. Then it turns into soft dough, then hard dough, while the heads bend and turn golden. PalayCheck advises you to harvest by hand when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. With a combine, wait for 90 to 95 percent.

You do not need to count the days by hand. The [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) tool in anee.io shows each lot's stage on any date you pick, what to do and what to watch for.
From palay to rice: drying, milling and recovery

Palay to rice takes three steps: drying, hulling and polishing. First dry the grain to 12 to 14 percent moisture within 12 to 24 hours after threshing, as PalayCheck advises. Wet grain left in a pile heats up, turns yellow and mills badly.

Then the mill removes the hull, and a polisher strips off the bran. The share of milled rice you get back is the milling recovery. Since November 2024 the PSA uses 63.0 percent as its official rate. Before that it used 65.4 percent.

blocks.caption: What 1,000 kg of dry palay gives at the PSA milling recovery rate of 63 percent

blocks.text:
So one cavan of palay, about 50 kg, gives about 31.5 kg of milled rice at that rate. Timing counts as well. PalayCheck notes that harvesting too early can drop milling recovery to as low as 53 percent.

For the palay price today and the palay price per kilo today by region, read our [palay price guide](/blog/palay-price-philippines). It also compares rice and palay price levels in the Philippines, so you can check a buyer's offer before you sell.
Rice seeds and seed classes

Good rice seeds are the cheapest yield booster you can buy. According to PalayCheck, high quality seed with at least 85 percent germination can raise yield by 10 percent or more. In the Philippines the Bureau of Plant Industry's National Seed Quality Control Services (BPI NSQCS) tests seed lots and tags them. The tag color tells you the class.

rows: Kept by the breeder, planted to make foundation seed
Grown by selected seed growers to make certified seed
Planted by farmers for the palay crop

blocks.text:
Buy certified palay seeds from accredited seed growers and check that the tag is valid. If you keep your own seed from last season's rice crop, run a germination test before sowing, as PalayCheck recommends.

Each new rice variety in the Philippines, or rice breed as some people say, gets a code from the National Seed Industry Council, such as NSIC Rc 222. PhilRice's free Binhing Palay app lists registered varieties and their traits. For the Philippine rice variety list, with inbred and rice hybrid picks side by side, see our [rice varieties guide](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines). It also covers Jackpot rice variety maturity and the rice variety characteristics of NSIC Rc 402, two things farmers often ask about.
What a palay picture or palay image shows
Many people look for a palay image for school, a report or a seed label. Here is what each growth stage looks like, so you can tell which one a photo shows.

items: **Young field:** flooded paddies with rows of pale green palay seedlings, set out at 18 to 21 days old.
**Tillering:** thick clumps of bright green leaves, with water still standing between the hills.
**Heading and flowering:** heads pushing out past the flag leaf, with tiny flowers open along each head.
**Ripening:** heavy heads bent over, turning from green to golden yellow.
**After threshing:** golden grain spread on concrete to dry, or packed in sacks.

blocks.text: If you need to draw one instead, a palayan drawing usually shows these paddies with dikes, a carabao, a small hut and mountains behind. Our [Palayan, Nueva Ecija page](/blog/palayan-nueva-ecija) gives a simple plan you can follow.

blocks.title: Dry before you sell
blocks.text: Fresh grain from the harvester carries 20 to 25 percent moisture in the wet season, PalayCheck notes. Buyers pay less for wet grain because part of what you sell is water. So dry it to 14 percent if you can store it safely.
Growing palay well: where to go next

Our Filipino guide to [pagtatanim ng palay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-palay) walks through every step, from punla to pag aani ng palay. It covers the seedbed, direct seeding with tools like the palatak palay seeder, water, abono timing and the treser ng palay at harvest.

Weeds and pests take the rest of your yield if you let them. PalayCheck says to control weeds in the first 45 days, so watch for grasses, broadleaves and any sedge weed such as Cyperus iria. After that, watch for the [rice insects](/problems/rice-insects) that come with each stage. For nutrients, start with our guide to [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice).

items.a: Palay in English is paddy, rough rice or unhusked rice. Bigas is milled rice and kanin is cooked rice.

items.q: What is the difference between palay and rice?
items.a: Palay still has its hull. Rice, or bigas, is the grain after the mill removes the hull and the bran. At the PSA rate of 63 percent, 100 kg of dry palay gives about 63 kg of milled rice.

items.q: How many days does palay take to grow?
items.a: IRRI groups short duration varieties at 100 to 120 days and medium ones at 120 to 140 days. Popular inbreds such as NSIC Rc 216 at 112 days and Rc 222 at 114 days after sowing are short duration.

items.q: How do I know if rice seeds are certified?
items.a: Look for a valid blue BPI NSQCS tag on the sack, and buy from accredited seed growers or through your DA office.

items.q: How much rice does one cavan of palay make?
items.a: A cavan of palay weighs about 50 kg. At the PSA milling recovery rate of 63 percent, that gives about 31.5 kg of milled rice. Your mill, the variety and the dryness of the grain change the result.
